result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_connected_watts_strogatz_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Watts-Strogatz small-world graph that is guaranteed to be connected. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_connected_watts_strogatz_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a Watts-Strogatz small-world graph that is guaranteed to be connected. title: >- [Graph.add_connected_watts_strogatz_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a Watts-Strogatz small-world graph that is guaranteed to be connected. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Watts-Strogatz small-world graph that is guaranteed to be connected. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10527-L10632){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_connected_watts_strogatz_graph( n, k, p, tries=100, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Connected Watts-Strogatz graph](../assets/graphs/add-connected-watts-strogatz-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three connected Watts-Strogatz graphs on a ring of eight nodes with k=4 and rewiring probability p=0, 0.2, and 1. At p=0 every node links to its two nearest neighbors on each side; rewired edges show as accent-colored shortcuts, 3 at p=0.2 and 9 at p=1. Every panel keeps all 16 edges and is connected, because a disconnected draw is retried." width="100%"} Draws the same graph as `add_smallworld_graph()`: a ring lattice in which each node is joined to its `k` nearest neighbors, with each edge rewired to a random node with probability `p`. If the result is disconnected, the graph is drawn again, continuing the same random stream, up to `tries=` times. With the same `seed=`, the first draw is the graph that `add_smallworld_graph()` builds, so the two agree whenever that graph is connected. The process follows NetworkX's `connected_watts_strogatz_graph()`. In a directed graph each lattice edge points around the ring from a node to the ones after it, and a rewired edge keeps its source, as in `add_smallworld_graph()`. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Connected Watts-Strogatz graphs are useful for: - small-world experiments that measure path lengths, which are only defined on a connected graph - spreading and synchronization studies in which every node must be reachable - comparing against `add_newman_watts_strogatz_graph()`, which adds shortcuts instead of moving edges ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nearest neighbors each node is joined to in the ring lattice. Must be even and less than `n=`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of rewiring each edge, between `0` and `1`. [tries]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of graphs to draw before giving up. Default is `100`. Must be at least `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k=` is odd or not less than `n=`, `p=` is not between `0` and `1`, `tries=` is less than `1`, or no connected graph turns up in `tries=` draws (always the case for `k=0` with more than one node). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Even with heavy rewiring, the graph comes out connected: ::: {#4f09e69f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_connected_watts_strogatz_graph(n=40, k=2, p=0.6, seed=1) graph.count_edges(), graph.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (40, True) ``` ::: ::: `add_smallworld_graph()` with the same seed gives a graph that has fallen apart, which is why a redraw was needed here: ::: {#6405fb29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=40, k=2, p=0.6, seed=1).is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
